content:
Daniel Okafor-Reyes
Backend Software Engineer | Java, Spring Boot, Event-Driven Services

Lisbon, Portugal | daniel.okafor-reyes@example.com | +351 555 010 202 | linkedin.com/in/daniel-okafor-reyes-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend engineer with 7 years of professional experience building and operating backend services in Java, a comparable language to Python. Experienced in REST API design, relational databases, Kafka-based event processing, automated testing, and CI/CD. Has deployed services to AWS EKS and improved production API performance, reliability, and data integrity.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: Java (8–17), Kotlin (basic)
Backend and APIs: Spring Boot, Spring MVC, Spring Data JPA, Hibernate, REST, OpenAPI
Databases and caching: PostgreSQL, Oracle, Redis
Messaging: Kafka, RabbitMQ
Cloud and delivery: AWS (EKS, S3, SQS), Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Jenkins
Testing and tools: JUnit 5, Testcontainers, Git, Linux

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Backend Engineer | Tejo Insurance Tech | Lisbon
Jan 2022–Present
- Develop and maintain seven Java 17 / Spring Boot microservices for policy quoting and claims intake.
- Designed and versioned the REST API for partner quoting, documented with OpenAPI and used by 12 broker partners.
- Produce and consume Kafka events for the claims workflow; introduced idempotent consumers and an outbox table to eliminate duplicate claim records.
- Reduced quote-endpoint p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds by adding Redis caching and resolving JPA N+1 queries.
- Deploy services to Kubernetes on AWS EKS using Helm charts and Jenkins pipelines; participate in an on-call rota one week per month.

Software Developer | Viajar Online S.A. | Porto
Sep 2019–Dec 2021
- Built booking and payment features in a Java 11 / Spring MVC monolith backed by Oracle.
- Wrote integration tests with Testcontainers, increasing payments-module test coverage from 35% to 70%.
- Contributed to splitting the monolith by extracting the notifications service using Spring Boot and RabbitMQ.

Junior Developer (Internship, then Full-time) | CodeFarol Lda | Porto
Jul 2018–Aug 2019
- Maintained PHP and later Java applications for small business clients.

EDUCATION
BSc Informatics Engineering | Atlantic Polytechnic Institute | 2018

LANGUAGES
English (fluent), Portuguese (fluent), Spanish (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, concise, professional CV with clear section headings, reverse-chronological experience, measurable outcomes, and relevant technical detail. The strongest evidence includes the 75% reduction in quote-endpoint p99 latency, the 35% to 70% test-coverage increase, Kafka event processing, API ownership, AWS EKS deployment, and on-call experience. The main content weakness is that the Professional Summary contains slightly awkward wording—particularly “a comparable language to Python”—and the CV does not clearly distinguish hands-on experience from skills listed without context.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional headings, plain text, readable dates, standard bullet points, and searchable keywords such as Java, Spring Boot, REST, PostgreSQL, Docker, AWS, EKS, Kubernetes, Kafka, automated testing, and CI/CD-related Jenkins experience. Parsing and AI-screening probability should be high for the core backend requirements and especially strong for Java, REST APIs, Kafka, AWS, Kubernetes, testing, and performance engineering. Screening may be weaker for Python/FastAPI, PostgreSQL depth, schema migrations, GitHub Actions, observability, logistics, and Dutch/French because these are either not supported by the candidate information or are not demonstrated in the CV. Do not add those terms as claimed experience unless they are truthful.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns very well with the role’s accepted comparable-language requirement: the candidate has 7 years of Java backend experience, including Spring Boot microservices, REST API design, Kafka, relational databases, Docker, AWS EKS, Kubernetes, automated testing, CI/CD pipelines, and production on-call work. It also aligns with the company’s ownership and reliability culture through deployment responsibility, latency improvement, idempotent consumers, duplicate-record prevention, and on-call participation. The principal candidate-side gaps are mainly Python/FastAPI, demonstrated PostgreSQL query tuning and schema migrations, logistics or supply-chain experience, observability tooling, Terraform, and Dutch or French. These are gaps in the candidate material rather than defects that can be fixed by rewriting the CV. The CV also does not explicitly demonstrate explaining technical trade-offs, although the technical accomplishments imply relevant engineering judgment.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES: None identified; the document does not contain a clear unsupported skill, tool, certification, or experience claim when cross-checked against the Original Candidate Information.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace “Backend engineer with 7 years of professional experience building backend services in Java, a comparable language to Python.” with “Backend engineer with 7 years of professional experience designing, building, and operating Java backend services.” This removes awkward wording and avoids making the CV sound as though it is explaining the job advertisement.
2. In the Professional Summary, replace “Has deployed services to AWS EKS and improved production API performance, reliability, and data integrity.” with “Deploys services to AWS EKS and has improved production API performance, reliability, and data integrity.” This uses a consistent professional voice and avoids the sentence fragment-like construction.
3. In the Technical Skills section, keep “Jenkins” but label the category more explicitly as “CI/CD and delivery: AWS (EKS, S3, SQS), Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Jenkins.” This makes the existing CI/CD evidence easier for ATS and recruiters to identify without claiming GitHub Actions experience.
4. In the Backend Engineer experience entry at Tejo Insurance Tech, change “Produce and consume Kafka events” to “Produce and consume Kafka events for claims workflow processing.” This uses the job’s event-ingestion and event-streaming terminology while remaining fully supported by the original candidate information.
5. In the same Tejo Insurance Tech entry, change “introduced idempotent consumers and an outbox table to eliminate duplicate claim records” to “introduced idempotent consumers and an outbox table, eliminating duplicate claim records.” This is more concise and preserves the measurable reliability outcome.
6. In the Software Developer entry at Viajar Online S.A., change “Contributed to splitting the monolith by extracting the notifications service using Spring Boot and RabbitMQ.” to “Contributed to monolith decomposition by extracting a notifications service with Spring Boot and RabbitMQ.” This more directly matches the job’s language around service architecture while remaining truthful.
